newsitem.title: USA: Stocks soar; Dow sets another record high.
newsitem.headline: Stocks soar; Dow sets another record high.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks rocketed Monday, lifting the Dow Jones industrial average to another record high as Wall Street bet the Federal Reserve will keep interest rates unchanged at a policy-setting meeting next week.
The Dow closed up 123.22 points, or 1.72 percent, at 7,292.75, beating by a wide margin its May 6 record finish of 7,225.32.
In the broader market, advancing issues beat declines 1,766 to 760 on moderate volume of about 459 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Standard & Poor's 500 Index also set an all-time high, adding 12.88 points to 837.66, and the NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 6.34 to 435.57, also a new high.
The dollar's slump to its lowest level against the Japanese yen since January also buoyed sentiment, fuelling hopes that a cheaper currency would boost the earnings of multi-national companies.

Among multi-nationals, General Electric Co. gained 1-3/4 to 59-7/8 in heavy trading after a stock split. Walt Disney Co., rose 2-1/4 at 84-1/2, DuPont Co., was up 2-1/2 at 110-5/8, Merck & Co. added 2-5/8 at 92-5/8 and Procter & Gamble was up 1-7/8 at 133-3/4.

Analysts said the market was less concerned that the Fed would raise interest rates again at its next policy-setting meeting on May 20. The Fed raised interest rates by a quarter point March 25 in a pre-emptive move against inflation.
"I think it's still the growing perception that the Fed is not going to raise rates," said John Church, chief investment officer at Glenmede Trust Co.
On Wednesday, the government will report on the Producer Price Index for April, and the current forecast is for a drop of 0.1 percent after another decrease of 0.1 percent in March.
In the bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury was up 2/32, leaving its yield steady at 6.89 percent.
But whether stocks can hold the gains in the face of several key economic reports this week is questionable.

"We could have a problem. If the numbers come in strong, stocks will lose these gains. And if there is evidence of a weakening, people could start to worry about corporate earnings," said Henry Herrmann, president and chief investment officer at Waddell & Reed.
On Tuesday, retail sales are due, with economists forecasting a 0.3 percent drop on average, and on Thursday, the Consumer Price Index for April.
The rally in blue chips was not matched by smaller stocks, as traders felt more secure in the big-name companies.

"We're seeing continuing demand for big-name first-tier stocks. Today was a continuation of the bullish trend, but small cap stocks may not have the follow-through," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist for Prime Charter Ltd.
"One to 2 percent swings in the Dow are becoming very commonplace these days," he said.

Oil stocks rallied as crude oil prices hit the highest level in two months, partly due to tension in the Persian Gulf after a U.S. military commander pledged to defend the strategic Strait of Hormuz amid new Iranian wargames in the Gulf. June crude oil closed up 95 cents at $21.38 a barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange.
Chevron Corp. hit a new 52-week high, adding 1-5/8 to 72 and Exxon Corp. rose 1-1/2 to 59-3/8.

International Business Machines Corp. jumped 4-3/8 to 171-7/8. The gain came after IBM scored a major publicity coup over the weekend when its Deep Blue supercomputer made chess history by defeating world champion Garry Kasparov.
On the Nasdaq, Citrix Systems Inc. surged after Microsoft Corp. agreed to license its software technology and include it in upcoming versions of Microsoft Windows NT.
Citrix was up 13-3/8 at 32-5/8, leading the list of most active Nasdaq shares, while Microsoft rose 1-3/8 at 118-1/8.
Among other technology shares, Cisco Systems Inc. closed up 1-5/16 at 62-15/16, Netscape Communications Corp. rose 3-5/8 at 35-3/4 and Gateway 2000 was up 1-1/4 at 63-3/4.
The stock of British consumer products company Grand Metropolitan Plc, the owner of Burger King, jumped 4-3/4 to 38-7/8 on the NYSE after it said it would merge with brewer Guinness Plc.
The Nasdaq Composite index gained 9.14 points to 1,344.19. The American Stock Exchange index was up 4.69 to 578.47.
The average NYSE share was up 63 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a record 7,885.875 up 104.763 or 1.35 percent.
